name: CSL Limited
executive_summary: CSL Limited is a global biopharma leader in plasma-derived therapies (CSL Behring), influenza vaccines (Seqirus), and specialty pharmaceuticals (including Vifor), now screening as a **buy** after a severe share-price de-rating. The quantitative screen flags cheapness (P/E 13.6, P/B 2.2), dividend yield (3.5%), and balance-sheet resilience across six of 22 models, but reported ROE of 6.7% reflects goodwill-heavy equity and recent impairment charges rather than normalised franchise economics. The valuation hook is a durable, oligopolistic plasma franchise trading at a cyclical-industrial multiple after FY2026 guidance cuts and flagged US$5–6.9bn writedowns. The central debate is whether plasma volumes, China pricing, and Vifor underperformance are adequately priced, or whether restructuring (Seqirus separation, cost cuts, buybacks) will restore earnings faster than the market expects. **Primary ASX filing body extracts are absent from the research library**; financial analysis below falls back to Yahoo annual data through FY2025, with interim FY2026 deterioration sourced from news headlines only.
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, CSL presents a quality-at-a-discount setup: the screen passes six models across five factor families—**cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk**—with a composite score of 64%, sector-relative score of 63%, and persistent buy conviction over four weeks (screen conviction 61%). Passed models include Neff PEGY (PEGY ≈ 0.05), Magic Formula, Dreman Contrarian, Piotroski F-Score, Dividend Growth, and Financial Health. At P/E 13.6 and yield 3.5%, the market is pricing CSL closer to a cyclical name than a biopharma compounder, despite FY2022–FY2025 revenue growth from US$10.5bn to US$15.4bn (Yahoo fallback) and FY2025 free cash flow of US$2.5bn supporting dividends and debt reduction.

Business quality remains structurally attractive. CSL Behring holds a leading global plasma fractionation position with high barriers to entry; Seqirus is a top-tier influenza vaccine franchise; and the pipeline offers optionality. Management is responding to margin pressure with workforce reductions (~3,000 jobs), plasma-centre rationalisation, and a planned Seqirus spin-off—actions consistent with protecting returns on capital rather than growth at any price. The buy case rests on mean reversion in plasma collections, a Vifor turnaround, and capital return (ongoing buyback plus ~3.5% yield) cushioning shareholders through transition. Conviction is tempered by the screen’s −80.1% reported earnings growth (distorted by the FY2026 impairment cycle) and depressed ROE, which suggest trailing metrics may lag forward reality—or may accurately reflect a broken growth narrative if impairments prove structural.
financial_review:
**Primary filings gap:** `filings_index.json` (regime: `asx_announcements`, fetched 25 Jul 2026) records **zero annual and zero interim filings**, three “other” market-commentary items (Market Index evening wraps, Feb–Apr 2026), and **zero downloadable body extracts** under `filings/bodies/`. Body refetch was attempted on all three indexed items; none yielded extractable text. All figures below are sourced from **`financials_annual.json` (Yahoo fallback)** unless noted as news-derived.

**Income statement trend (FY2022–FY2025, Yahoo fallback, US$m unless stated):**

| Metric | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Revenue | 10,493 | 13,174 | 14,690 | 15,430 |
| Gross profit | 5,664 | 6,708 | 7,561 | 7,951 |
| Operating income | 2,316 | 2,102 | 2,764 | 2,959 |
| EBITDA | 3,465 | 3,902 | 4,733 | 5,134 |
| Net income | 2,255 | 2,194 | 2,642 | 3,002 |
| Diluted EPS (US$) | 4.80 | 4.53 | 5.45 | 6.17 |
| R&D | 1,156 | 1,235 | 1,430 | 1,359 |

Revenue compounded at roughly 14% annually over four years, driven by the Vifor acquisition (FY2023 investing cash outflow of US$10.5bn for business purchase per cash-flow statement) and organic plasma/vaccine growth. Gross margin compressed from 54.0% to 51.5% as cost of revenue rose to US$7.48bn in FY2025; operating margin stabilised near 19%. Net income and EPS rebounded in FY2024–FY2025 after a FY2023 dip linked to integration costs and higher interest expense (US$393m in FY2025 vs US$143m in FY2022).

**Balance sheet (FY2025, Yahoo fallback):** Total assets US$39.4bn; goodwill and intangibles US$16.2bn (post-Vifor); tangible book value US$3.2bn (was negative US$660m in FY2023); total equity US$19.3bn; **net debt US$7.7bn** (down from US$8.9bn in FY2024); total debt US$11.5bn. Net debt/EBITDA ≈ **1.5×** on FY2025 EBITDA—manageable for an investment-grade issuer if FY2026 EBITDA holds. Inventory rose to US$6.5bn (from US$4.3bn in FY2022), consistent with plasma working-capital intensity. Employee benefit and pension liabilities total roughly US$600m (non-current US$366m plus current pension US$234m).

**Cash flow (Yahoo fallback):** FY2025 free cash flow **US$2.54bn** (operating cash US$3.56bn less capex US$1.02bn), up from US$1.51bn in FY2024 and US$909m in FY2023 (Vifor-acquisition year). Dividends paid US$1.43bn; net long-term debt reduction US$735m.

**Interim / recent period (news only — no filing bodies):** Yahoo `quarterly_income` contains a single half-year snapshot (revenue US$8.21bn, net income US$2.01bn, diluted EPS US$4.13; period label “2024” in source—likely H1 FY2025). **No verified interim filing extract is available.** News headlines report that H1 FY2026 net profit fell ~81% (“Earnings call transcript: CSL Limited reports 81% profit drop amid strategic shifts in H1 2026”, 10 Feb 2026), and that management subsequently cut full-year revenue and profit outlook while flagging ~US$5bn impairments (“CSL Plunges 22% After Cutting Outlook And Flagging $5 Billion Impairments”, 11 May 2026) and a US$6.9bn writedown with a blown-out turnaround timeline (“CSL shares bleed to decade low after $6.9 billion writedown as turnaround timeline blows out”, 11 May 2026). These events are **not reflected** in the Yahoo annual series, which ends at FY2025 (June year-end). The financial review therefore has a **material forward-looking gap** that cannot be closed without primary ASX announcement or annual-report extracts.
risks_and_flags:
**Earnings and impairment cycle:** The May 2026 outlook downgrade and US$5–6.9bn impairment flags (news) suggest goodwill and asset values—particularly Vifor and possibly plasma-related assets—may be overstated relative to revised cash-flow assumptions. Without primary filing language on contingencies, asset impairments, or going concern, severity cannot be verified from bodies; this remains a headline-level red flag.

**Plasma collection and margin pressure:** News links the guidance cut to weaker plasma volumes, collection-centre closures, and margin compression. Plasma supply is cyclical and capital-intensive; restructuring may improve unit economics but risks volume disruption during transition. The 15 Jul 2026 simplywall.st piece explicitly frames “margin pressures, impairments and leadership shifts” as having changed the investment story.

**China pricing:** Repeated news references to China pricing pressure on immunoglobulin and albumin products pose a structural headwind to one of CSL’s growth markets.

**Vifor integration:** The FY2023 acquisition added ~US$10.5bn of purchase consideration and ~US$16bn of intangibles on the balance sheet. Underperformance here is a core driver of the impairment narrative and ROE suppression (6.7% on screen).

**Leverage and pension:** Net debt of US$7.7bn and total debt of US$11.5bn (FY2025 Yahoo) are serviceable at current EBITDA but become less comfortable if FY2026 EBITDA falls sharply post-impairment. Non-current pension/post-retirement obligations of US$366m plus current pension items of US$234m warrant monitoring; **no covenant or going-concern detail is available from filing bodies**.

**Governance and execution:** CEO changes announced 10 Feb 2026 (“CSL Limited Announces Chief Executive Officer Changes”, marketscreener.com) introduce leadership transition risk during a complex restructure and Seqirus separation. Restructuring announcements—workforce cuts, centre closures, Seqirus spin-off (“CSL Restructure And Seqirus Split Reset Expectations After Share Price Slide”, 2 May 2026; “One of the world’s largest biotech firms, CSL to cut 3,000 Jobs and spin off its vaccine unit”, 19 Aug 2025)—carry execution and separation-cost risk.

**Competitive/regulatory:** Industry headlines on rare-disease immunology (e.g. European regulator review of Amgen’s Tavneos, 26 Jun 2026) underscore regulatory sensitivity in adjacent therapeutic areas, though not directly CSL-specific.

**Data quality:** Absence of ASX annual reports and interim results in the library prevents verification of impairment triggers, segment disclosures, or management commentary on covenants and going concern. The `gap_fill_source_map.json` confirms filings_bodies and macro_context as thin evidence layers.

- **11 May 2026:** “CSL Plunges 22% After Cutting Outlook And Flagging $5 Billion Impairments” (Yahoo Finance); “CSL shares bleed to decade low after $6.9 billion writedown as turnaround timeline blows out” (Business News Australia)—full-year guidance cut; plasma, China, and Vifor cited.
- **12 May 2026:** “CSL: No more excuses” (intelligentinvestor.com.au)—critical fundamental tone.
- **30 Mar 2026:** “CSL says it’s pivoting to shake off its sluggish ways and find growth” (AFR)—strategic pivot narrative.
- **Jun–Jul 2026:** Partial recovery theme—“CSL Shares Bounce 20% off Lows” (thebull.com.au, 11 Jun 2026); “Up 36%: Can CSL shares keep rebounding?” (Motley Fool, 10 Jul 2026); “Down 55% in a year: Do brokers still rate CSL shares as a buy?” (Motley Fool, 22 Jul 2026); “CSL (CSL.AX) shares rebound A$16 billion off lows” (TechStock², 19 Jul 2026).

Strategy has shifted from acquisitive growth (Vifor) to portfolio simplification (Seqirus spin), cost reduction, and buyback-supported returns. No M&A beyond internal restructuring is flagged in the manifest.
research_rationale: Deep research confirms the quantitative screen’s cheapness and capital-return support but cannot verify FY2026 impairment severity or forward earnings without primary filings, leaving the buy case intact on valuation yet materially unresolved on earnings quality.
